title: Automated routing policy rollback guardrails + anti-flap logic
creator: Miles Thornton
description:
Context
Today, we can trigger failover based on noisy signals and partially automated policies, but rollback behavior is inconsistent and (in worst cases) oscillates during partial outages. This ticket implements the rollback semantics + guardrails from ADR-043 and hardens the automation controller/policy engine integration so we (a) can safely revert to primary, (b) can prevent rapid back-and-forth flips, and (c) can keep on-call in control with clear audit trails.

Links
- ADR-043: Automated routing policy rollback: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback.json
- Runbook usability requirements (draft): sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/routing-policy-failover-controller-runbook.json
- Related work: ENG-2415 (dry-run), ENG-2412 (trigger hierarchy), ENG-2413 (region health service)

Problem statement
During impairment events, signal quality changes over time (network reachability, regional brownouts, capacity exhaustion). If we revert too early, we can re-expose customers to a still-broken region; if we revert too late, we prolong elevated latency/cost in the failover region. Without anti-flap controls, repeated policy flips can cause cascading overload, confuse debugging, and destroy confidence in automation.

Goals / acceptance criteria
1) Deterministic rollback evaluation
- Given the same inputs (signals + config), the controller computes the same rollback decision.
- Rollback decisions include explicit rationale + evidence signals.

2) Anti-flap safeguards (per ADR-043)
- Hold-down timer: once a route/model/tenant tier fails over, do not allow rollback or re-failover for a configurable minimum window (default 10m), unless forced by operator.
- Rate limit: configurable max policy flips per scope (default 2/hour per route + tier; stricter for Dedicated).
- Hysteresis: rollback requires stronger “healthy” evidence than the initial failover trigger required (e.g., N consecutive healthy windows + burn rate below threshold).

3) Safe automation boundaries
- Per-tenant safety limits: blast-radius constraints (e.g., automation can’t flip >X% of a tier’s traffic in <Y minutes unless explicitly approved).
- Dedicated constraints: rollback must respect pool drain state and capacity headroom gates (no rollback if target region is below headroom threshold).

4) Clear on-call UX + audit
- All automated flip and rollback actions emit structured audit events (who/what/why) and post a concise summary to incident-bot.
- Runbook includes explicit ‘how to stop the bleeding’ steps: freeze automation, revert to last-known-good, increase hold-down.

Non-goals
- Changing customer-facing SLA language.
- Replacing all routing policies; this is focused on rollback/anti-flap logic for failover automation.

Implementation plan
A) Policy state machine (controller)
- Introduce explicit states per (route, model, tier, region-pair):
  - NORMAL (primary)
  - FAILED_OVER (secondary)
  - ROLLBACK_PENDING (eligible but waiting for corroboration / timers)
  - ROLLED_BACK (recently reverted; hold-down applies)
  - FROZEN (manual override; automation disabled)
- Persist last decision + timestamps to prevent controller restarts from “forgetting” hold-down windows.

B) Guardrails
- Hold-down timers:
  - failover_hold_down_seconds (default 600)
  - rollback_hold_down_seconds (default 600)
- Hysteresis parameters:
  - rollback_requires_consecutive_healthy_windows (default 3)
  - rollback_max_error_burn (default 0.1x)
  - rollback_max_p95_latency_burn (default 0.25x)
- Rate limits:
  - max_policy_flips_per_hour_per_scope (default 2)
  - if exceeded -> freeze scope + page on-call (action required)

C) Determinism + ordering
- Canonical evaluation order: reachability -> 5xx burn -> tail latency burn -> capacity headroom -> control plane health (per ADR-042/043 alignment).
- Normalize missing signal behavior:
  - Missing authoritative signal should not trigger rollback; treat as “unknown”, keep current state, and emit warning + metric.

D) Audit + observability
- Emit events:
  - failover.recommendation
  - failover.execution
  - failover.rollback_recommendation
  - failover.rollback_execution
  - failover.freeze_scope
- Add metrics (low-cardinality labels only):
  - failover_policy_flips_total{scope,tier,reason}
  - failover_scope_frozen_total{scope,tier}
  - failover_hold_down_active{scope,tier}
- Add alerting annotation text that includes the hold-down + rate-limit status.

Testing plan
- Unit tests
  - state machine transitions (including controller restart simulation)
  - hold-down timer enforcement
  - rate limit enforcement + freeze behavior
  - hysteresis (healthy windows) logic
- Integration tests (staging)
  - scripted signal playback: failover -> partial recovery -> rollback eligibility -> rollback
  - “noisy signals” playback to validate no oscillation
  - missing signal stream (e.g., capacity signal absent) should not crash; should not rollback
- Game day readiness checks
  - dry-run output includes: eligible rollback scopes, blocked-by timer, blocked-by rate-limit, and evidence signals

Rollout plan
- Stage 0: land code behind feature flags; default OFF for prod.
- Stage 1: enable in staging for rehearsals (limited routes/models).
- Stage 2: prod enable for internal-only canary tenant + lowest tier traffic (Hosted) with manual approval hooks still enabled.
- Stage 3: expand to more routes/models + Dedicated (after validating drain-state gating and headroom thresholds).

Risks / open questions
- Hold-down defaults may be too conservative (slower rollback) or too aggressive (oscillation). We’ll tune based on burn-rate + probe evidence during game days.
- Dedicated pool drain coordination: need a clear contract for “safe to rollback” when drain is partially complete.
- On-call confusion risk: must ensure dashboards show ‘blocked by hold-down / rate-limit’ clearly.

Definition of done
- Guardrails implemented + documented in runbook.
- Audit events emitted and visible in incident timeline tooling.
- Staging rehearsal shows no oscillation under noisy signals.
- At least one controlled production test uses the new rollback guardrails with success criteria met.
updates: 2026-01-06 (Benji Okafor): Started implementation based on ADR-043. Added controller-side hold-down + rate limit scaffolding. Next: persist decision state to avoid restart-induced flaps; coordinate with Devon for incident-bot summary format.

2026-01-10 (Miles Thornton): Please ensure ‘missing signal’ is treated as UNKNOWN (no rollback) rather than default healthy/unhealthy. We saw a controller crash in rehearsal when a stream was absent; deterministic + safe default is critical.

2026-01-13 (Allison Grant): Observability note: keep labels low-cardinality. Use tier + scope enums; avoid tenant_id. Add a single ‘reason’ enum that maps to ADR hierarchy (reachability/5xx_burn/latency_burn/capacity/unknown).

2026-01-15 (Benji Okafor): Implemented freeze-on-rate-limit exceeded. Proposed behavior: if exceeded for a scope, freeze automation for that scope and page on-call with remediation steps (increase hold-down, verify signals, or manual override).

2026-01-17 (Rafael Mendes): On-call usability requirement: the controller must expose “why not rolling back” (hold-down remaining, insufficient healthy windows, headroom gate). Please ensure dry-run output includes these blockers so the runbook flow is straightforward.

2026-01-24 (Benji Okafor): Staging integration tests passing for oscillation scenarios. Added persistence of last_action_ts and last_state to controller store. Added canonical evaluation ordering to prevent non-deterministic outcomes across instances.
2026-02-03 (Benji Okafor): Rolled out to prod internal canary under feature flag + approval hooks. No unexpected flips; verified hold-down enforcement via simulated signal playback endpoint.

2026-02-12 (Miles Thornton): Marking Done. Guardrails shipped and enabled for game day routes; audit events now appear in incident timeline. Follow-up: tune defaults post next game day + ensure dashboards annotate frozen scopes (tracked in ENG-2426).
